clue.text: Lancer told to choose an entrance

indicators.note: told means the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: to choose an entrance is to pick a door

explanation.surface: A soldier with a lance is being instructed to pick which way in he goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick a door', said aloud, gives the bullfighting word.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the horseman in a bullfight who goads the bull with a lance.

clue.text: Agent cut up for bowel problem

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an agent is a spy
to lop is to cut

explanation.surface: A secret agent is chopped up, causing intestinal trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SPYLOP backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyps are small growths in the lining of the colon, a common bowel complaint.

clue.text: Magpie? Five to feature in my papers

indicators.note: to feature in means the numeral is set within the other letters

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise like 'my!'
ID means identity papers
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A magpie appearing in five of my newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, British COR. The question mark marks the magpie as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Corvids are the crow family, and the magpie is one member of it.

clue.text: Dines out with song to provide some realism

indicators.note: out means the letters of dines are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a chant is a song

explanation.surface: Someone eats out and sings, bringing a dose of reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINES into DISEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To disenchant is to free from illusion, so it gives someone a dose of reality.

clue.text: 2 given intravenously

indicators.note: given suggests what is handed over inside the following word

explanation.surface: Two doses administered by drip into a vein.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' points to the answer at 2 down, CORVID; the raven is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Went down as a result of what happened in a gastric haemorrhage

parts.note: gastric relates to the stomach, informally the tum
in a haemorrhage blood flows, so something bled

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed because of internal bleeding in the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The stomach (TUM) BLED is what happens in a gastric haemorrhage.
explanation.definitionFit: To tumble is to fall, so 'went down' is a straight synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Like Bob Dylan in blue and brown, heartlessly plugged out

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: out means the shortened letters are thrown into disorder
heartlessly means the central letter of plugged is removed

explanation.surface: Dylan in a blue and brown outfit is unplugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' drops the central G of PLUGGED; 'out' rearranges the remaining PLUGED into GLEDUP. Tangled Up in Blue is a Bob Dylan song.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan's song title says he is tangled up in blue, so that is what he is like.

clue.text: New motion, top item to be debated

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh motion at a meeting, the leading item for debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges MOTION TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is a question open to argument, an issue up for debate.

clue.text: Oliver is having one portion? Must be feeling queasy

indicators.note: a portion is a part, so the answer is a part of these words

explanation.surface: Oliver Twist asks for a single helping and must feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'Oliver is having'.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverish means slightly sick or bilious, as if the liver were upset.

clue.text: One little and quiet place to sleep on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a dorm is a dormitory, a place to sleep
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A small, quiet place to stay overnight beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England. 'One little and quiet' plays on 'quiet as a mouse'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse is a tiny rodent, and mice are proverbially quiet.

clue.text: House sold off around mid-April

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the middle letter
off means the letters of sold are spoiled and rearranged
mid picks the central letter of the word April

explanation.surface: A house was sold at some point in the middle of April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles SOLD to LODS, and 'around' puts it round R, the middle of APRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament, the House of Lords.

clue.text: City is suitable for everyone involved in commercial vehicle insurance

parts.note: a van is a commercial vehicle

indicators.note: involved in means one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: insurance is cover
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A city's van insurance is said to be suitable for all drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a large Canadian port on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Girl, nine, starts wearing ponytail twisted in an affecting manner

indicators.note: wearing means the outer letters have the initials inside them
twisted means the letters of ponytail are rearranged
starts takes the opening letters of girl and nine

explanation.surface: A nine-year-old girl in a twisted ponytail looks touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' scrambles only the ponytail; 'wearing' puts the 'starts' of Girl and nine inside it, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignant describes something that moves the emotions, so the adverb means movingly.

clue.text: Writer having a change of heart and spirit

indicators.note: a change of heart here means the central letters of the pen swap places

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes

explanation.surface: An author changes their mind and their mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the middle letters IR of BIRO round to RI. Biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vivacity or vigour, the spirit in a lively performance.

clue.text: Me, 21, grappling with a PhD in population studies

indicators.note: grappling with suggests a struggle that jumbles the letters

parts.note: 21 across is the answer gory

explanation.surface: A bloody academic wrestles with a doctorate on populations.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' stands for the answer at 21 across, GORY; 'grappling with' rearranges ME GORY A PHD.
explanation.definitionFit: Demography is the statistical study of human populations, births, deaths and so on.

clue.text: That guy talks to turbans?

parts.note: that guy is he
to address someone is to talk to them

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a man who speaks to his turbans.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that turbans are only examples of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbans are one kind of headwear, an example of items worn on the head.

clue.text: One on the tail of pair planning lurid hijacking

indicators.note: on the tail of means the numeral follows right behind the shuffled letters
planning means the letters of pair are organised into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lurid can mean racy, sensational

explanation.surface: A lurid plot devised by a pair, with someone at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the tail of' puts the Roman one right behind the scrambled pair; 'lurid' is not an anagram signal here but a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Air piracy is the seizing of an aircraft, otherwise called hijacking.

clue.text: Criminal unclothed to reveal somebody with no special powers

indicators.note: to reveal means taking the clothes off shows what sits inside them

parts.note: unclothed says the answer has outer letters, its clothes, which come off; they are not clued and must be read from the answer
a muggle, in the Harry Potter books, is a person without magic

explanation.surface: A criminal strips off and is revealed to be powerless.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: strip the answer of its outer S and R, its 'clothes', to reveal MUGGLE, J. K. Rowling's word for a non-magical person. The clothes letters are not clued.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler is a lawbreaker who moves contraband across borders illegally.

clue.text: Refusing food when a refusal reportedly damages you

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: reportedly means what follows is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: in casual speech, damages you is wrecks ya

explanation.surface: Refusing to eat because a refusal harms you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' tells you WRECKS YA is a sound only: spoken it gives REXIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorexia is the eating disorder in which a person will not eat enough.

clue.text: Staff working to prop organisation, but not too much

parts.note: to staff is to man
working means switched on

indicators.note: organisation means the letters of to prop are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Employees are working to support a company, though not excessively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' arranges TO PROP as TROPPO. The answer is the Italian musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In a musical score the Italian marking qualifies a tempo, translating literally as 'but not too much'.

clue.text: Complete and utter European

indicators.note: utter means to say aloud, so the word for the European is heard

parts.note: a Finnish person is a European

explanation.surface: A wholly complete and total European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like an adjective for 'European' but means speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish is to complete a task, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Digestive movement with vigour

parts.note: pep is vigour
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A digestive biscuit moved with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digestive' looks like the British biscuit, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Peptic means relating to digestion, as in a peptic ulcer.

clue.text: Bloody half of literary device

indicators.note: half of here takes the back four of eight letters

parts.note: allegory is a literary device

explanation.surface: A curse about half of some literary technique.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of ALLEGORY is the answer. 'Bloody' looks like a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gory means covered in or full of blood, as in a gory film.

clue.text: Deceptive advocacy of dire perils and sin

indicators.note: dire means terrible, so the letters of perils are put in a bad state

parts.note: a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: A warning about the awful dangers and wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' rearranges PERILS into LIPSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip service is support professed in words but not meant, insincere backing.

clue.text: Expensive soak in marinade

definitions.meaning: to ... food is to soak it in liquid

explanation.surface: Costly to soak something in a marinade.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep means both overpriced and to immerse something in liquid.

clue.text: 2 involved in murder

definitions.meaning: the answer at 2 down is corvid, a family including this bird
a group of ... is called a murder

explanation.surface: Two people mixed up in a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: The crow is a corvid, and crows gather in a flock known as a murder.

clue.text: Leaving us can make it relax and wallow

indicators.note: can make means the letters are reworked to form the result

parts.note: us is read as U's, two copies of the letter U

explanation.surface: Leaving the group may help someone relax and indulge themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'us' as U's: the clue says the answer, 'Leaving' its two Us, 'can make' the anagram fodder that follows. 'relax' looks like part of the definition but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To luxuriate is to indulge oneself in pleasure, to wallow in comfort.

clue.text: See 6
Route to get 'bravo' out of theatre land

indicators.note: out of here means a letter is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: Broadway is New York's theatre district
B is bravo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A way to hear applause from the theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: Bravo looks like a cheer from the audience, but it is B in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadway is the part of a road used by vehicles, a route.

clue.text: Medium or perhaps strong? You can have instant coffee at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Choosing between medium and strong coffee, with instant offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium or perhaps strong' reads like coffee strengths; 'perhaps' is the first piece of the initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium is someone claiming to contact the dead, a person with supposed psychic powers.
